name: Lý Công Uẩn
role: Vị vua khai sáng nhà Lý
interpretation: A Vietnamese emperor in his mid-thirties, sturdy and broad-shouldered, with a full round face and calm, firm eyes. Black hair drawn into a topknot under a dark lacquered court hat with a flat back, a trimmed black moustache and short beard. He wears a layered silk court robe in deep yellow with wide sleeves and dragon roundels at the chest, a dark under-robe at the collar, and a jade-set leather belt; his signature accessory is the jade-ornamented belt clasp.
known_facts: Born in 974 at Co Phap, in what is now Bac Ninh province.
Rose to command the palace guard under the Early Le dynasty before taking the throne.
In 1009, after the death of Le Long Dinh, he was enthroned by the court and founded the Ly dynasty.
In 1010 he moved the capital from Hoa Lu to Dai La and renamed it Thang Long.
The move was proclaimed in the Chieu doi do, the edict on moving the capital.
His era name was Thuan Thien; he patronised Buddhism and built many pagodas.
He died in 1028 and was succeeded by his son Ly Thai Tong.
unknowns: No contemporary portrait or description of his face and build survives; the appearance is reconstructed from Ly-era court dress conventions.
The names and status of his parents and the story of his adoption are recorded only in later, semi-legendary chronicles.
The text of the Chieu doi do survives only through later compilations, so its wording is not certainly original.
